plain.li: Sand in my bread, sand in my boots, sand in my bed. Saw something worth seeing today, though.
The heat broke at sundown and I sat on the wall until the stars came out. They come out fast here.
[hot] Too hot to work after noon. Too hot to sleep. Too hot to write much.
Learned something about living out here today. The dry country has its own rules, and I'm still learning them.
[night] Cold enough at night to see my breath, in the same place that nearly cooked me at noon.

warm.li: Out here every bit of shade is shared. I like that about the place.

cheerful.li: The sky out here at night! I didn't know there were that many stars.

gloomy.li: Everything out here is trying to dry out, including me.

cold.li: Water is the only thing that matters out here. I've started measuring the day in cups.

plain.li: Snow up to my knees and still coming. Saw tracks I didn't know, and followed them.
[morning] Everything frozen and quiet this morning. My breath hung in the air like smoke.
Learned a trick against the cold today. My feet have been warm all day.
The cold out here gets into your teeth. The animals manage. I'm working on it.
[snow] Snowed all day. The world went white and small.

warm.li: Somebody showed me how to keep warm today, for nothing. I'll pass it on.

cheerful.li: Fresh snow this morning and I was the first one out in it!

gloomy.li: The winters here are long. This one has hardly started.

cold.li: The wind matters more than the cold. Dress for the wind.

plain.li: Everything here is wet, or growing, or both. Saw something in the green today that watched me back.
[rain] Rain again. Rain yesterday. Rain tomorrow, I expect. Learned how to keep some of it off, at least.
[night] The marsh is louder at night than the colony is by day. I lay awake listening to it.
My boots haven't been dry since we came here. My feet have given up hoping.

warm.li: The green out here is full of life. Every time I look closely, something is looking back.

cheerful.li: Learned how to make a rain cape out of leaves! It even works, mostly.

gloomy.li: Something moves out in the reeds every night. I've stopped asking what.

cold.li: This land rots anything you leave on the ground for a week. Keep things off the floor.

plain.li: Looked up from my work today and there was something on the ridge, watching the valley. Then it was gone over the top.
Heard about the high passes today. I'd like to see the top of these mountains one day.
[morning] The sun hits the peaks an hour before it reaches us. I watched it come down the slope.
Found a crack in the rock with cold air coming out of it. Didn't go in. Thought about it all day.

warm.li: The mountains make everything we build look small, and I don't mind.

cheerful.li: Shouted across the valley today and the mountain shouted back!

gloomy.li: The mountains were here long before us and won't notice when we're gone.

cold.li: High ground is good ground. We can see them coming from a long way off.

plain.li: Walked the shore at low tide. The sea leaves something different on the sand every day.
Got a shell today. It's on the sill by my bed now, and I keep picking it up.
[storm] Watched the sea in the storm. The waves came up the rocks higher than the roof.
[fog] Sea fog all morning. I could hear the waves and nothing else.

warm.li: There's salt on everything here, even the bread. I've stopped minding.

blunt.li: Sea's rough today. So am I.

cheerful.li: Held a shell to my ear and heard the sea in it, even with the real sea right there!

gloomy.li: The sea takes whatever is left near it. One day it'll take the shore path, and then the field above it.

cold.li: The tide comes in twice a day. Plan the shore work around it.

plain.li: [rain] Sat out the rain in a doorway with my animal and watched the yard turn into a pond.
[storm] Thunder all night. Neither of us slept, my animal and me, so we kept each other company.
[snow] My animal had never seen snow come down this hard. Neither had I. It was wonderful.
[fog] Something came at me out of the fog today. Only an animal. My heart took the rest of the morning to settle.

warm.li: [storm] My animal was frightened of the storm, so I sat with it until it passed. I think I needed it as much as it did.

blunt.li: [rain] Wet day. Animal wet too. We waited it out.

cheerful.li: [snow] Snowball fight with an animal. The animal won.

gloomy.li: [fog] The fog makes everything look like it's coming for you. Most of it isn't.

cold.li: [storm] Animals take storms badly. Mine settles faster with someone sitting by it. Worth knowing.
